name: Should I choose a curbless shower for my primary bathroom?

mainEntity.name: Is a curbless walk-in shower worth it in a primary bathroom remodel, or does it create drainage and waterproofing problems?
mainEntity.text: Is a curbless walk-in shower worth it in a primary bathroom remodel, or does it create drainage and waterproofing problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: A curbless shower is often one of the most popular luxury upgrades in a primary bathroom remodel because it creates a seamless look and makes the room feel more open. It can also improve accessibility, especially if you want fewer barriers between the shower and the rest of the bathroom. The tradeoff is that the shower requires very careful slope design, waterproofing, and drain placement. This feature should usually be planned as part of a full remodel, since the floor structure and shower pan details matter a lot. If the room is small or the subfloor conditions are challenging, the design needs to be engineered properly to avoid drainage problems. Homeowners should ask how the contractor handles waterproofing transitions, inspection steps, and water containment. A curbless shower can be a great upgrade, but only when the build quality is excellent.
acceptedAnswer.description: A curbless shower can give a primary bathroom a cleaner, more luxury look and improve accessibility, but it requires precise slope, waterproofing, and drain planning. It is best done during a full remodel, not as a simple cosmetic update. Poorly executed curbless showers can leak or leave standing water.
